summary: Capture Comet's fourth-AI review and close the safe autonomous items: defence procurement carve-out on About, wage policy rationale refinement, editor recusal policy, utils.js FROZEN SURFACE guard.

items.headline: Comet Round 2 review captured
items.body: docs/Comet-Review-Round2-2026-05-23.md captures Comet's fourth-AI review at v5.62. Confirms editor disclosure as complete enough for journalism citation, the v5.58 excluded-coverage rationale as defensible and honest, and the v5.61 source threading as the right discipline. Identifies the next-tier rigor work as per-criterion operationalization (per-lever status criteria for Economic Policy, per-component checklists for Ethics, exact combination arithmetic for Flagship Delivery). Surfaces Immigration as the only dimension untouched across the v5.58 to v5.62 arc and the dimension with the least cross-ideological source balance. Session cut off mid-section 7.

items.headline: Defence procurement added to About boundary statement
items.body: The About 'what this does not grade' list and rationale now explicitly name specific defence procurement contracts (fighter jets, naval vessels, Arctic surveillance) as not graded as a separate file. The Defence & Trade construct uses NATO spending percentage and trade diversification as its measurable outcomes; specific procurement contracts would fit the Major Projects model and may move there if the Defence & Trade tripwire forces the dimension to split. Closes one of two new gaps Comet's Round 2 review surfaced.

items.headline: Wage policy rationale refined for cross-dimension footprint
items.body: The About boundary rationale paragraph for public-sector bargaining was expanded to note that Treasury Board agreements touch three dimensions at once: Fiscal Health through workforce reduction, Economic Policy Response through wage dynamics, and Immigration through workforce planning. The labour-relations file as a whole does not have its own grade because Treasury Board agreement timing is intermittent and the cross-dimension footprint would risk double-counting. Closes Comet Round 2's finding that the prior one-line treatment undersold the complexity.

items.headline: Editor recusal policy added
items.body: The About Editor and Disclosures section now includes a Recusal policy line stating that if a future conflict of interest arises (paid relationship with a graded entity, federal-department contract, board seat with a policy-affected organization), the affected dimension will be flagged in the next changelog entry with the nature of the conflict and the editorial response. The flag stays on the dimension card until the conflict is resolved. Closes Comet Round 2's last-gap finding on the editor disclosure surface.

items.headline: utils.js FROZEN SURFACE comment block added
items.body: src/utils.js now opens with a FROZEN SURFACE comment block per CLAUDE.md operational guardrails. The comment names the functions affected (gpaToGrade, computeOverallGPA, computeHouseholdGPA, gpaPointsForGrade, headline-score rounding) and the four-step protocol a future agent must follow before changing them. Closes Comet's repeated finding that a future agent editing utils.js would have no programmatic signal that the GPA formula is frozen. No logic changed.

summary: Three Perplexity-recommended institutional sources added to Economic Policy and Affordability source pools; two more (CER, OAG) carried forward to June for Climate source-band rebalance.

items.headline: Perplexity third-AI review captured
items.body: docs/Perplexity-Review-2026-05.md captures Perplexity's bundle-attached review of the dashboard at v5.60. Reaches a positive headline verdict ('Yes, genuinely') on whether the dashboard is credibly non-partisan, while flagging source-diversity gaps in Climate, Affordability, and Economic Policy as the persistent credibility ceiling. The review surfaces three-of-three convergence with the prior Grok and Comet reviews on source diversity as the load-bearing remaining gap. Perplexity's top five additions are listed with priority order, two of which are blocked by the CLAUDE.md ten-source ceiling on Climate.

items.headline: Three institutional sources added (Perplexity priorities 2, 3, 5)
items.body: Economic Policy Response sources[] adds Centre for the Study of Living Standards (Canadian Productivity Review) as the reference point for independent productivity analysis, and Conference Board of Canada (productivity and competitiveness research) as a centrist economic research voice. Affordability Response sources[] adds Food Banks Canada (Hunger Count) as floor-level affordability evidence that is impossible to dismiss as politically motivated, and Conference Board of Canada (economic and consumer research) as the centrist research voice. Both dimensions now sit at 10 sources, at the CLAUDE.md ceiling. Threading the new sources into specific grade-moving up/down triggers is June 2026 work under Bias-Resistance Discipline B.

items.headline: CER and OAG carried to June for Climate source-band rebalance
items.body: Perplexity's top two Climate recommendations (Canada Energy Regulator's Energy Future projections, Office of the Auditor General's climate program audits) are blocked from this commit because Climate is already at the 10-source CLAUDE.md ceiling. June 2026 cycle should evaluate trimming duplicates (CCI appears twice; ECCC departmental plans appear twice) and then add CER and OAG together. Both pass the 'impossible to call partisan' test and would close the most-cited remaining bias-surface gap.

summary: Climate and Affordability now thread specific market-oriented challenge sources into the metric evidence, without changing grades.

items.headline: Challenge sources threaded into metric evidence
items.body: Climate & Environment now replaces generic Fraser Institute and Macdonald-Laurier source-family pages with specific EV-mandate and energy-policy analyses, then attaches them to the EV mandate and emissions-cap metrics. Affordability Response now attaches the Fraser Institute GST / groceries-benefit critique to the Grocery benefit metric and keeps Retail Council as grocery-sector context. CFIB stays in the recurring scan but is not retained on the card until a future cycle finds exact trigger-level support. No grades, thresholds, formulas, or GPA weights changed.

summary: Skeptic Path and safeguards jumps now move directly to their target sections on desktop and phone-width layouts.

items.headline: In-page trust jumps fixed
items.body: The Skeptic Path controls now use native in-page anchors with compact link hit boxes, so they land on the rule, triggers, metrics, sources, or critic / defender section on desktop and phone-width layouts. The header's read-the-safeguards control now waits for the Rubric view to render before jumping to the Methodology & Safeguards panel.

summary: Close the four remaining open items from the May AI-review panel: editor disclosure, scope-exclusion rationale, past-versions visibility, and right-of-centre source additions to Climate and Affordability.

items.headline: Editor and Disclosures section added to About
items.body: The About tab now opens with a named editor disclosure: editor identity (Chris Sawatsky, a Calgary-based enterprise-software consultant), political affiliation (none — no party membership, no campaign donations on file in the coverage period), professional conflicts (no paid consulting with graded entities, no current federal contract), funding (unfunded; Buttondown and GoatCounter paid out of pocket), AI assistance (named tools used for drafting and audits; grading decisions made by the human editor against the published rubric), and corrections process (GitHub issues route to the editor per the published Corrections and Right of Reply policies). Closes the editor-disclosure gap flagged in two-of-two convergence by the Grok (2026-05-17) and Comet (2026-05-23) AI reviews.

items.headline: Excluded coverage areas now carry a published rationale
items.body: The About 'What This Scores and What It Does Not' section now explains why each excluded area (Indigenous reconciliation, healthcare federal-provincial transfers, public-sector bargaining, pre-designation pipeline announcements, foreign policy beyond defence and trade) is not currently a standalone grade. Reasons name source-coordination constraints, federal-scope boundaries, and the maturity of monthly-cadence indicators. Closes Comet's Section 3 finding that the boundary statement named the exclusions without giving a rationale a reader could evaluate.

items.headline: Past Versions and Snapshots surfaced on About
items.body: A new Past Versions section on the About tab points readers to the Change Log tab, the GitHub commit history with per-file diffs, the data folder at any specific commit (so a reader can load the dashboard state at any past cycle), and the per-cycle closure memos in docs/. Closes the version-archive gap flagged in two-of-two convergence by the Grok and Comet reviews.

items.headline: Right-of-centre and industry sources added to Climate and Affordability
items.body: Climate & Environment sources[] now includes Fraser Institute (environment publications) and Macdonald-Laurier Institute (energy and natural resources) as right-of-centre and energy-sector independent challenge sources. Affordability Response sources[] now includes CFIB (research and economic analysis) and Retail Council of Canada (grocery and food) as industry and business-group challenge sources. These additions surface the source pool to readers immediately; threading them into specific grade-moving up/down triggers happens in the June 2026 cycle under bias-resistance Discipline B (thread existing challenge sources before adding new). Closes the source-diversity gap flagged by Comet in Section 4.

summary: Comet review follow-up tightened scope copy, Skeptic Path anchors, and three methodology explanations without changing grades.

items.headline: Comet review follow-up
items.body: The safe follow-up from Comet's third independent review is now reflected in the live data and UI. Affordability Response leads with the scope caveat before the tariff burden, Defence & Trade now says it does not grade broader foreign policy posture, Economic Policy enumerates the five core levers inside the scoring criteria, Ethics & Transparency defines the five disclosure-machinery components, and Flagship Delivery clarifies that its Combination Rule is status-count based rather than an arithmetic average. The About boundary now names several important files that are not standalone grades in this version, including Indigenous reconciliation, healthcare transfers, public-sector bargaining, pre-designation pipeline announcements, and broader foreign policy.

items.headline: Skeptic Path source jump tightened
items.body: The cited-sources, metrics, scoring, and critics / defenders targets now carry scroll margins so the Skeptic Path links land with the section heading visible instead of overshooting on desktop.

summary: Comet (Perplexity) third independent AI review captured. Confirms two prior gaps and surfaces specific methodology, source-diversity, and code-quality findings for the June 2026 cycle.

items.headline: Comet review logged with 2-of-2 convergence on prior findings
items.body: docs/Comet-Review-2026-05.md captures Comet's bundle-attached review of the dashboard at v5.56, run 2026-05-23. The review confirms the editor disclosure surface gap (2-of-2 convergence with the 2026-05-17 Grok probe) and refines the version archive finding (Change Log exists for changes; reader-facing full-state snapshot archive does not). New methodology-rigor findings worth acting on in June: enumerate Economic Policy 'core levers', publish Ethics disclosure-machinery checklist, publish Flagship Delivery derivation arithmetic. New coverage findings: Indigenous reconciliation needs either a 12th dimension or an explicit boundary statement; foreign policy beyond NATO needs a one-line scope caveat on Defence & Trade; wage policy needs a one-line About note. New source-diversity findings: Climate & Environment grade-moving chain has no right-leaning or energy-sector source; Affordability Response has no industry analysis; Immigration has no independent challenge from pro-immigration or restrictionist sources. New UX/code findings: anchor link #4 (sources) overshoots scroll target; DimensionCard timing-based scroll is fragile; no automated test for POCKETBOOK_DIMS / excludeFromGPA consistency; no test guarding the utils.js GPA frozen surface. Comet's session cut off mid-section 10 before completing the closing paragraph; the captured text is otherwise substantively complete. Bundle approach (tmp/perplexity-bundle.md v2 with React components) worked as designed; no fabricated citations detected.

summary: Source-to-trigger audit for the May 2026 cycle published, with 1 grade move documented and 6 trigger-source gaps carried forward to the June cycle.

items.headline: Source-to-trigger audit identifies 6 evidence gaps
items.body: docs/Source-To-Trigger-Audit-2026-05.md cross-references each of the 11 graded dimensions' pre-committed up and down triggers against what the May 2026 cycle actually checked. Headline: 1 grade move (Fiscal Health D to C, PBO Spring Economic Update assessment), 4 holds with explicit trigger evaluation (Major Projects, Housing down-direction, Ethics, Flagship combination rule), 6 holds with at least one trigger source that was not evaluated in the cycle record. The 6 gaps are specific: Defence 3.5% pathway after the 2026-03-26 NATO 2% confirmation, Affordability gas-tax-suspension up-trigger ($500/household threshold), Housing up-direction vs. the 2026-03-30 Canada-Ontario Housing Partnership, Climate event-driven sources untouched after the 2026-04-19 D+ to D move, Carbon Pricing CCI/ECCC sources untouched, Immigration temporary-resident share against the 5% target. None of these are claims that a grade is wrong; they are claims that the cycle record does not show the trigger was evaluated. June 2026 cycle carries each as a one-line check.

items.headline: Per-cycle source-to-trigger pass added to pre-cycle checklist
items.body: docs/Bias-Resistance-Protocol.md pre-cycle checklist now asks for one line per graded dimension stating whether the trigger fired, was considered and not fired, or was not checked, with rationale. The May audit found this discipline was missing across most dimensions. Protocol bumped to v1.3.

summary: AI verification methodology added as a standing trust artifact, codifying a three-model persona panel with a verbatim-quote anti-confabulation rule.

items.headline: AI verification methodology published
items.body: docs/AI-Verification-Methodology.md captures a standing three-model persona panel approach (ChatGPT with browsing, Claude with web tools, Gemini) crossed against four reader personas (federal political journalist, nonprofit policy analyst, civic teacher, skeptical voter). The prompt template requires verbatim quotes with location so AI confabulation can be caught when models present paraphrase as quotation. Convergence rules cut signal from noise: 3-of-3 model agreement is a real signal worth carrying forward, 2-of-3 is a candidate, 1-of-3 is a single-model artifact noted but not acted on. The first single-model probe (Grok, 2026-05-17) surfaced two real findings for the June 2026 cycle (editor disclosure surface, version archive visibility) plus one methodology gap (the confabulation pattern that drove the verbatim-quote rule). Pairs with docs/Perceived-Bias-Survey.md (human responses) and docs/Validation-Sprint-Templates.md (human outreach). Suggested cadence is once per quarter plus after major UI or rubric changes; not a per-cycle requirement.

items.headline: Bias-resistance protocol reconciled to v1.2
items.body: docs/Bias-Resistance-Protocol.md public-surface list now includes the AI verification methodology as item 8 and updates the status markers for the v5.41 to v5.55 work: the Skeptic Path anchor-link fix in v5.51, the saved axe-core artifact at docs/accessibility/axe-v5.46.json, and the two expanded-drawer accessibility findings carrying forward to June 2026. No principles changes.

summary: Validation sprint outreach templates adapted from the LaunchSims feedback report and adjusted to the dashboard's voice rules.

items.headline: Validation sprint templates published
items.body: docs/Validation-Sprint-Templates.md adapts the outreach templates from the LaunchSims DeepSim report (launchsims.com/en/share/deepsim/ds_YT_PTw_RLUo2) for the audience-validation sprint LaunchSims recommended. The original templates contained fabricated performance claims ('zero partisan bias complaints from all major party groups,' '72% of early nonprofit analyst users say...') and a non-existent 'institutional access pass' offer. Both were stripped. The rewrite drops press-release register for individual-asking-for-feedback voice and replaces invented social proof with named methodology artifacts recipients can actually verify. Two templates: one for federal political beat journalists, one for nonprofit advocacy policy analysts. Includes outreach mechanics (target list, batching, response classification, pass/fail decision criteria) and explicit limits. Cross-referenced from docs/Bias-Resistance-Protocol.md (public-surface backlog item 7) and docs/Perceived-Bias-Survey.md (new recruiting respondents section). Pairs with the perceived-bias survey methodology so the editor now has both the recruit-readers side and the collect-responses side of audience validation.

summary: May 16 source recertification added as a separate retrospective source-health artifact.

items.headline: May 16 source recertification
items.body: A retrospective Tier 3 source recertification now checks the May 16 dashboard snapshot pinned to dimensions.json at 60a2e6e. The pass logged 114 unique URLs, saved the link-check artifact, found no grade-chain blocker, and carried three Promise Delivery 404s forward as June link-repair candidates without changing May grades, sources, thresholds, or the May ledger.

summary: Header trust-frame alignment fixed and the safeguards link now jumps directly to the Methodology & Safeguards panel.

items.headline: Trust-frame link layout fixed
items.body: The new 'read the safeguards' control in the header trust frame used a normal button minimum target, which made it render like a large boxed control and broke the desktop column alignment. It is now a text-link button with compact sizing, the three desktop columns use fixed equal tracks, and the click scrolls directly to the Methodology & Safeguards panel instead of only switching tabs. Desktop and phone-width smoke checks confirmed the frame aligns, stacks cleanly, and has no horizontal overflow.

summary: Skeptic Path anchor links now jump reliably inside expanded dimension drawers on desktop and mobile.

items.headline: Skeptic Path links fixed
items.body: The Skeptic Path links at the top of each dimension drawer now use one shared jump handler that prevents the card wrapper from swallowing the click, waits for React state updates, and scrolls to the target section. The 'what would move the grade' target now exists inside the main scoring panel, and the critic / defender link opens its collapsed section before scrolling. Desktop and phone-width smoke checks confirmed all five links land on their intended sections.

summary: Closure memo version history catches up to v5.50, including two newly surfaced axe-core findings that appear only when dimension drawers are expanded.

items.headline: Closure memo v1.2 — version history catch-up
items.body: docs/Bias-Resistance-Cycle-2026-05-Closure.md version history now references v5.47, v5.48, and v5.49 as companion commits that landed after the original closure memo at v5.46. Records that none change the bias-resistance arc's scope, and adds explicit documentation of two new axe-core findings that surface only when dimension drawers are expanded: Event badge contrast (#e65100 on #fff3e0 = 3.45:1, introduced by v5.48's Event badges) and a nested-interactive flag on the DimensionCard wrapper (technically present since v5.40 but only visible to axe when inner buttons are rendered). Both flagged for the June cycle. The earlier saved axe snapshot (docs/accessibility/axe-v5.46.json) used the closed-drawer state which is still clean.

summary: Link-rot scanner gains retry-with-fallback for User-Agent anti-bot mismatches. ChatGPT-flagged CBC false positives now correctly resolve as live.

items.headline: Link-rot scanner now retries blocked URLs with browser User-Agent
items.body: ChatGPT's dry-run cross-check (recorded in 4171b7f) confirmed that two CBC URLs flagged as broken by the link-rot scan actually load 200 in a normal browser. Root cause: CBC anti-bots the scanner's descriptive UA ('Canada Under Carney monthly fetch'). check_url_with_wayback now tries the descriptive UA first (works for most sources including .gc.ca and most RSS), then retries with a real-browser Safari UA if the primary probe fails. URLs that respond live on the browser-UA retry are marked live with a 'primary UA blocked; live on browser-UA retry' note. Tested: CBC URLs now correctly resolve as live; the descriptive-UA-friendly sources (.gc.ca, RSS feeds) keep their existing behavior. Closes the scanner-identity-rot false positive class without introducing regressions for descriptive-UA-friendly hosts.

summary: Trust-surface pass: the live dashboard now points readers to safeguards sooner, labels event-driven triggers, summarizes key context inside each drawer, and adds a grade-challenge guide.

items.headline: Methodology safeguards surfaced earlier
items.body: The header trust frame now tells readers how to check the dashboard and jumps directly to the Rubric tab. The Rubric tab now opens with a Methodology & Safeguards link panel pointing to the scoring rubric, source register, source authority map, bias-resistance protocol, sensitivity analysis, and the new grade-challenge guide.

items.headline: Dimension drawers add context and event labels
items.body: Expanded dimension cards now include a Key trade-offs & confounders section built from existing scope, attribution, lag, active adjustment, and inherited-context fields. Event-driven grade triggers now display an Event badge with a short explanation that the source family is known now and the specific URL gets added if the event happens.

items.headline: How To Challenge A Grade guide added
items.body: docs/How-To-Challenge-A-Grade.md gives readers a plain route for checking or contesting a grade: walk the rule, trigger, metric, source, and critic / defender views, then choose correction, trigger disagreement, missing evidence, or judgment disagreement. Linked from the Rubric tab and About page.

summary: Closure memo verification-layer cleanup after ChatGPT review: git log range fixed to be inclusive, live-version check corrected for SPA bundle, axe-core result now backed by saved JSON artifact, and three narrative inconsistencies tightened.

items.headline: Closure memo verification layer fixed (six findings addressed)
items.body: ChatGPT's review of the v5.46 closure memo identified six issues with the verification layer. All fixed in v5.47: (1) git log range used 'A..B' syntax which excludes A; corrected to 'A^..B' for the inclusive 20-commit arc. (2) Removed broken 'v5.* tag' references since the repo does not use git tags. (3) Live-version curl was greping static HTML, but the SPA version is in the JS bundle; replaced with a two-step bundle-extract approach. (4) Saved an axe-core JSON snapshot (docs/accessibility/axe-v5.46.json) with reproduction instructions, so the '0 violations' claim is now backed by a reproducible artifact rather than oral assertion. (5) TL;DR said 'two passes' of accessibility work; corrected to 'five iterative passes' to match the detailed track description. (6) 'WCAG AA aligned across dashboard' softened to 'automated axe-core checks clean; manual assistive-tech testing pending' since real screen-reader and assistive-tech testing has not been performed. Plus 'All 4 Phase 1 fixes' clarified as 'five named fixes across four approval groups' to remove cold-reader confusion.

items.headline: Axe-core snapshot artifact added
items.body: docs/accessibility/axe-v5.46.json saves the axe-core 4.10.2 run against live v5.46. Contains the full counts (0 violations, 1 incomplete, 24 passes, 37 inapplicable), the incomplete category detail (15 TrendArrow glyph spans with correct aria semantics), reproduction instructions, and a note that this supersedes the earlier oral claim.

summary: Closure memo published: docs/Bias-Resistance-Cycle-2026-05-Closure.md consolidates the 20-commit May 2026 arc into one authoritative reference for future reviewers.

items.headline: May 2026 bias-resistance cycle closure memo published
items.body: docs/Bias-Resistance-Cycle-2026-05-Closure.md is the single authoritative reference for the May 2026 bias-resistance + accessibility cycle. Covers all 20 commits (c35dec6 → e8be26b, v5.26 → v5.45) with hashes, dates, scope, per-track summary, current state matrix, what requires editor action vs what's done, quick verification commands, and a ready-to-paste ChatGPT closure-review prompt. Self-contained so future reviewers (human or AI) can read this one file and get the full picture without chasing conversation history. Live axe-core on v5.45: zero violations confirmed. Next cycle's closure memo should reference this one as prior baseline.

summary: Post-v5.44 axe-core re-run caught one remaining #888 contrast violation on the Approval Signal disapproval percentage; fixed plus three more #999/#aaa instances surfaced during the sweep.

items.headline: Final contrast cleanup after v5.44 deploy verification
items.body: Live axe-core 4.10 run against deployed v5.44 surfaced one remaining color-contrast violation: the Approval Signal '/ X%' disapproval percentage at #888 on white (3.54:1). That style block was in ApprovalSignal.jsx which the v5.43 sweep missed. Fixed plus three additional instances (two more #999 in ApprovalSignal.jsx, one #999 in ScoreDerivation.jsx, one #aaa in About.jsx) found in the follow-up grep. All replaced with #666 (5.7:1 on white) matching the documented --text-muted token in index.css.

summary: Skeptic Path orientation upgraded to threaded navigation: each of the five ingredients in the callout is now a clickable anchor jumping to its drawer section.

items.headline: Skeptic Path orientation gains anchor-jump navigation
items.body: The Skeptic Path callout at the top of every graded dimension drawer (added in v5.36) was prose-only orientation pointing readers at section names. v5.44 turns each of the five ingredients into a clickable anchor link with smooth-scroll behavior. A reader can now click '(1) the rule', '(2) what would move the grade', '(3) the evidence under each metric', '(4) the cited sources', or '(5) named critic and defender views' to jump directly to the relevant drawer section. Required adding stable id anchors to the Key Metrics, Source Links, the triggers section wrapper, and the perspectives section wrapper (the scoring section already had id=dim-${dim.id}-scoring). Closes the fuller Skeptic Path UI threading item from the bias-resistance audit's Section 7. Fuller restructure (e.g., a single-pane Skeptic Path view) remains future work.

summary: Axe-core run on live v5.41 surfaced 8 contrast violations outside the grade-chip palette. Inline-style text colors aligned to the documented contrast-tested token set.

items.headline: Inline text colors aligned to WCAG AA tokens
items.body: Live axe-core run against v5.41 confirmed the v5.41 grade-chip contrast fix landed clean but surfaced 8 additional contrast violations in inline-styled components: visitor-count pill (#888), scoreboard Promises card headline (old C-range #e68a00), various scoreboard captions and tracker text (#999), email-signup helper (#999), promise tracker timestamp (#aaa), and the #1a73e8 link blue on the #fafafa page background. The repository's index.css has documented contrast-tested tokens (--text-muted: #666 at 5.7:1 on white) and a warning that #888/#999 fail AA, but inline styles in components were drifting from this. This commit replaces inline #888, #999, #aaa, and #bbb (where used as text color) with #666 across DimensionCard, ScoreboardHeader, EmailSignup, PromiseTracker, CompareView, Methodology, About, and VisitorCount. The #1a73e8 link blue is replaced with #1565c0 (passes 4.5:1 on both #fff and #fafafa). The old C-range #e68a00 surfaced in the scoreboard Promises conditional-color path; replaced with #8d5a00 (the v5.41 chip C color).

summary: Bias-Resistance Protocol pre-cycle checklist gains viewport-check rule for UI-touching commits.

items.headline: Viewport-check discipline codified in the protocol
items.body: The pre-cycle checklist now includes: 'If the cycle includes any UI-touching commit: run a viewport-pass smoke check at both desktop (≥1024px) and phone-sized (≤414px) widths before declaring the commit complete.' Added after v5.40's keyboard-fix commit caught a mobile scoreboard overflow that desktop-only verification had missed. UI changes need explicit narrow-viewport verification before they ship.

summary: Accessibility audit Phase 2: grade chip contrast darkened to meet WCAG AA, skip-to-content link added, drawer focus management clarified per WAI-ARIA disclosure pattern.

items.headline: Grade chip colors darkened to meet WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1)
items.body: Seven of twelve grade chips failed WCAG 2.1 AA normal-text contrast: B+ (3.78), B (2.93), B- (2.31), C+ (3.15), C (2.47), C- (2.81), D+ (3.78). Foreground colors in src/constants.js GRADES were darkened to all-pass: B+ #3f6e24 (5.58), B #3a6822 (6.08), B- #33621e (6.66), C+ #9a6300 (4.75), C #8d5a00 (5.50), C- #9a4d00 (5.57), D+ #a52c0c (6.04). A, A-, D, D-, F were already passing and unchanged. Color hierarchy (green→yellow-green→orange→red) preserved. GPA values unchanged (grade math is a frozen surface; color is visual styling). Computation script reproducible: WCAG relative-luminance formula applied to sRGB-converted hex values.

items.headline: Skip-to-content link added to Dashboard
items.body: Dashboard.jsx now includes a 'Skip to main content' link at the top of the page, targeting #main-content (a tabIndex={-1} anchor before the scoreboard row). Visually hidden by default, visible on focus with a blue background at top-left. Satisfies WCAG 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks: keyboard users can bypass the header and tab navigation on first tab.

items.headline: Drawer focus management clarified per WAI-ARIA disclosure pattern
items.body: The accessibility audit's Finding 4 assumed focus should move into the drawer on expand. On closer reading of the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices Disclosure pattern, that assumption is incorrect for this widget type: focus correctly stays on the trigger when toggling. Current DimensionCard behavior (after v5.40's keyboard fix) matches the spec exactly. Finding 4 closed as a clarification, not a code change. Audit doc updated.

items.headline: Bias-Resistance Protocol pre-cycle checklist gains drift-check rule
items.body: The pre-cycle checklist now includes: 'If running a language, accessibility, or source audit: verify each finding against current code state, not against historical drift.' Added after the v5.40 audit-doc reconciliation found that two accessibility findings had already been fixed in code before the audit doc was written. Code-inspection passes need to cross-check current state.

summary: Bias-resistance docs reconciled to the v5.39 state, dimension cards now open by keyboard, and the mobile scoreboard no longer overflows narrow screens.

items.headline: Dimension cards keyboard access fixed
items.body: Dimension cards now expose button semantics, focusability, aria-expanded state, and Enter / Space keyboard activation on the card wrapper. This closes the high-severity accessibility finding that keyboard-only readers could not expand dimension drawers.

items.headline: Mobile scoreboard overflow tightened
items.body: The mobile header title now gets a fixed small-screen size, and the four headline cards stack to full width on phone-sized screens. This removes the horizontal overflow caught during the v5.40 viewport check.

items.headline: Bias-resistance closure docs reconciled
items.body: The May bias-resistance audit, Bias-Resistance Protocol, and accessibility audit now match the v5.39 reality: methodology FAQ, challenge-enabling hygiene, Skeptic Path orientation, perceived-bias survey methodology, full language audit, accessibility audit, and Phase 2 scaffold exist; survey activation, fuller Skeptic Path UI restructuring, remaining accessibility follow-ups, and the first substantive Phase 2 audit remain future work.

summary: Phase 2 foundational-methodology audit framework scaffolded. Annual-cadence doc frames three foundational questions (dimension choice, POCKETBOOK weighting, promise selection) for the first scheduled audit pass.

items.headline: Foundational methodology audit framework scaffolded
items.body: docs/Foundational-Methodology-Audit-2026.md frames the three foundational-bias questions that Phase 2 must answer when it runs (annually, or on rubric major version bump): why these 11 graded dimensions and not others, why these 4 in POCKETBOOK_DIMS and not others, how the 43 tracked promises were selected. The doc documents the audit's process (editor reflection, no script support, second-pair-of-eyes review), the three possible per-question outcomes (confirmed / documented / surface-bias finding), and the explicit constraint that foundational findings inform the NEXT rubric major version rather than changing the current rubric mid-cycle. Editor reflection deferred to first scheduled audit pass (2026 Q4 or 2027 Q1).

summary: Accessibility audit pass completed by code inspection. Seven findings (1 high, 5 medium, 1 informational); no fixes shipped this commit per Tier 1.4 scope.

items.headline: Accessibility audit doc published
items.body: docs/Accessibility-Audit-2026-05.md documents seven WCAG 2.1 AA findings from a code-inspection pass against src/components/*.jsx and src/constants.js. The high-severity finding: DimensionCard's outer wrapper is clickable but not keyboard-operable (missing role, tabIndex, onKeyDown). Five medium-severity findings cover grade-chip contrast verification, TrendArrow Unicode glyphs without aria-label, drawer focus management, inline button-styled divs in collapsible toggles, and missing skip-to-content link. One informational finding: color-as-primary-indicator is partially mitigated by letter grades and text labels. Closes Tier 1.4 of the bias-resistance plan. Full WCAG-AA conformance + accessibility statement remain Tier 3 work; this commit is the audit pass only.

summary: Perceived-bias survey methodology drafted and linked from About and the Methodology FAQ. Survey tests whether readers from different political priors can describe how a grade was reached, not whether they agree with it.

items.headline: Perceived-bias survey doc published
items.body: docs/Perceived-Bias-Survey.md documents the two-question survey format (comprehension test + party self-ID), pass/fail criteria adapted from the LaunchSims simulation analog (<25% bias-label from any major party = pass), the mechanism (GitHub Discussions preferred for openness, Buttondown fallback for privacy), how results will be published, and the explicit limits (voluntary participation, results are signal not statistically representative). Linked from About and the Methodology FAQ. Closes the perceived-bias-survey item in the Bias-Resistance Protocol's public-surface backlog. The actual survey activation (GitHub Discussions enable + first cycle's responses) is editor follow-on work.

summary: Skeptic Path orientation now sits at the top of every graded dimension drawer, naming the five ingredients a reader walks to challenge a grade.

items.headline: Skeptic Path orientation added to dimension drawers
items.body: Every graded dimension drawer now opens with a small Skeptic Path callout naming the five ingredients a reader walks to challenge a grade: (1) the rule, (2) what would move the grade, (3) the evidence under each metric, (4) the cited sources, (5) named critic and defender views. Tracker dimensions (Promise Delivery) do not display the callout. The drawer's existing sections already render in roughly this order; the callout names the path so a skeptical reader knows what they're looking at. Partial fix for the Section 7 Skeptic Path UI finding — fuller UI threading remains future work.

summary: Full 12-dimension language audit completed: the 'Judgment enters in X' framing and the 'grade is about Y, not Z' scope-disclaimer pattern hold uniformly across all graded dimensions.

items.headline: Section 4 of the bias-resistance audit extended to all 12 dimensions
items.body: The May 2026 bias-resistance audit's language section originally sampled 4 of 12 dimensions. The full pass on the remaining 8 (Major Projects, Fiscal Health, Affordability Response, Carbon Pricing Policy, Housing Supply, Ethics & Transparency, Flagship Delivery, Promise Delivery) confirms the framing language is consistent across all graded dimensions. No asymmetric tells, no one-sided hedging, no 'critics say'/'defenders argue' patterns. The 'Judgment enters in X' anchor and the 'The grade is about Y, not Z' scope-disclaimer pattern are party-symmetric devices applied uniformly. Section 4 closes as a green pass with no language-level fixes recommended this cycle.

summary: Methodology FAQ now lives in the Rubric tab, preempting eight common bias accusations with published trigger-language answers.

items.headline: Methodology FAQ added to the Rubric tab
items.body: Eight common questions are now answered inline in the Rubric tab: why grades vary across dimensions, why announcements do not always count as delivery, what would change a grade, why Approval Signal is excluded from the GPA, what the dashboard refuses to score, whether the rubric was adjusted after seeing results, how source diversity affects confidence, and whether the rubric itself could be biased. Each answer points to the published rule or the relevant doc rather than to editor judgment. Closes Tier 2.6 of the bias-resistance plan.

summary: Tier 1 challenge-enabling hygiene shipped: Corrections Policy, Right of Reply, and Cite As section all live and linked from About.

items.headline: Corrections Policy published
items.body: docs/Corrections-Policy.md documents what gets corrected vs re-graded, how to report a correction, the changelog 'type: correction' schema, the response timeline, and what corrections do not do. Linked from About. Closes the Tier 1 corrections-policy item per the bias-resistance plan.

items.headline: Right of Reply channel published
items.body: docs/Right-Of-Reply.md provides a documented channel for federal ministries, agencies, watchdogs, and named third-party analysts cited in any dimension's evidence chain to submit critiques. Documents who it's for, what it is not, the review process, what gets reflected, and the limits and scope. Linked from About. Closes the Tier 1 right-of-reply item.

items.headline: Cite As section added to About
items.body: About now includes a Cite As section providing a citation format for journalists, researchers, and other dashboards. Includes the dashboard URL, rubric version, and pointer to the open-source dimensions.json for per-dimension citations. Closes the Tier 1 citation-format item.

summary: Bias-Resistance-Protocol drafted: codifies eleven principles, three emergent disciplines, and pre/post-cycle review templates into a recurring methodology gate.

items.headline: Bias-Resistance Protocol v1.0 drafted
items.body: docs/Bias-Resistance-Protocol.md codifies what the May 2026 audit cycle learned. Eleven principles with built/partial/new status. Three new disciplines that emerged from this cycle's fixes: must-have-prior-substantive-view before adding a source, thread-existing-challenge-before-adding-new, and modifiers-explain-what-does-not-COUNT-not-what-should-not-HURT. Pre-cycle checklist, post-cycle review template, per-grade-move party-symmetry line, public-surface backlog, and audit re-run cadence. Reflects actual findings rather than preempted speculation per the planning doc's sequencing rule.

summary: Bias-resistance audit doc closed out as a true closure memo; raw audit output untracked to match its gitignore status.

items.headline: Bias-resistance audit doc now reads as closure memo
items.body: docs/Bias-Resistance-Audit-2026-05.md was written before the Phase 1 fixes shipped, so it read as forward-looking. The doc now opens with a Closure summary mapping all four shipped fixes to their version + commit references (v5.28 7b4136a, v5.29 b746abb, v5.30 b06e9de), each Fix section header carries a Shipped status, and Next steps now lists the actual follow-on work (Bias-Resistance-Protocol, Methodology FAQ, Tier 1 hygiene, full language audit, Skeptic Path UI, perceived-bias survey, Phase 2 foundational audit). No findings changed.

items.headline: Raw audit output untracked from git
items.body: scripts/output/ is gitignored by design. The raw audit output (scripts/output/bias-audit-raw-2026-05.txt) was tracked before the gitignore entry took effect; this commit untracks it to match the policy. The output remains regenerable via node scripts/audit-bias-resistance.mjs.

summary: Bias-resistance audit Fix 4 + Fix 5: event-driven trigger convention surfaced in methodology doc; Immigration modifier-absence documented as intentional.

items.headline: Trigger sourcing conventions documented in the scoring rubric
items.body: The methodology doc now explains the three trigger sourcing patterns (sourceUrl, internalRef, event-driven) so readers can interpret trigger panels correctly. Event-driven triggers are deliberate placeholders for source-families whose specific URLs become knowable only when the event occurs. Closes audit Fix 4: surface the convention rather than hide it.

items.headline: Immigration modifier absence documented as intentional
items.body: The Immigration dimension's judgmentDetail now explicitly states why no External Constraint modifier is applied: the absorption strain that prompted the correction was inherited from prior policy decisions, but the current government's response to those conditions is what this dimension grades. Prior conditions do not soften the assessment of current action. Closes audit Fix 5 in the conservative direction (document intent) rather than expansive direction (add a softening modifier).

summary: Bias-resistance audit Fix 3: defenders perspectives now cite named institutional sources, closing the critics-attributed / defenders-anonymous asymmetry on five dimensions.

items.headline: Defenders perspectives now name their authoritative sources
items.body: The audit found that five dimension defenders blocks cited zero or few named sources while critics blocks cited 2-6. Affordability Response, Carbon Pricing Policy, Climate & Environment, Housing Supply, and Economic Policy Response now bring named institutional sources into their defenders prose (PBO, OECD, CCI, CER, Department of Finance, Treasury Board Secretariat, CMHC, Smart Prosperity Institute) where authoritative defensive reasoning already supported the position. No grades, thresholds, or substantive claims changed; attribution surfaced.

summary: Bias-resistance audit Fix 1b + 1c: PBO independent challenge sources added to Immigration and Defence & Trade grade-moving chains.

items.headline: Immigration cites PBO Demographic Implications report
items.body: Added the PBO 'Demographic Implications of the 2026-2028 Immigration Levels Plan' (RP-2526-025-S) to the Immigration dimension's sources list and attached it as a sourceRef on the PR target (2026-2028) metric. Closes the audit finding that Immigration's grade-moving chain lacked an independent challenge source. No grade, threshold, formula, or modifier rule changed.

items.headline: Defence & Trade cites PBO Major Capital Priorities assessment
items.body: Added the PBO Spring Economic Update Major Capital Priorities assessment (NT-2627-003-S) to the Defence & Trade dimension's sources list and attached it as a sourceRef on the NATO spending (2025e) metric. PBO directly assesses Canadian defence funding adequacy including the NATO commitment. Closes the audit finding that Defence & Trade's grade-moving chain lacked an independent challenge source. No grade, threshold, formula, or modifier rule changed.

summary: Independent challenge sources now sit directly under key Major Projects and Climate metrics.

items.headline: Major Projects and Climate evidence chain tightened
items.body: Already-cited independent sources now appear under the specific Key Metrics they qualify. Major Projects threads Fraser Institute and Angus Reid into the headline-investment / credit-claiming metric; Climate & Environment threads CCI, IISD, CBC, and The Conversation into the emissions-pathway and ECCC-capacity metrics. No grades, thresholds, formulas, or source pool changed.

items.headline: Bias-resistance audit updated after Fix 1a
items.body: The audit raw output and findings doc now treat visible metric source links as grade-moving evidence. Major Projects and Climate & Environment no longer carry the no-independent-challenge flag; Defence & Trade and Immigration remain open for separate review.

summary: Ethics trigger traceability repaired and the first bias-resistance audit artifacts drafted.

items.headline: Ethics Annex A trigger now points to the working filing
items.body: The Ethics & Transparency up-trigger for the PM's Brookfield accounting now links to the Ethics Commissioner Annex A PDF already used in the dimension's source list, replacing the dead PMO backgrounder link.

items.headline: Bias-resistance audit artifacts drafted
items.body: A planning doc, reusable audit script, raw audit output, and first May bias-resistance audit now separate real methodology risks from script artifacts. The audit frames future fixes around threading existing challenge sources into grade-moving claims before adding new sources.

summary: May source-link sweep: nine broken citation URLs replaced with current canonical pages.

items.headline: Broken source links repaired across nine citations
items.body: The May link-rot scan flagged nine cited URLs returning 404. Replacements pulled from canonical equivalents on pm.gc.ca, canada.ca, climateinstitute.ca, fraserinstitute.org, and angusreid.org. Affected dimensions: Carbon Pricing Policy (consumer carbon price, industrial pricing), Fiscal Health (capital gains cancellation), Housing Supply (Canada-Ontario Partnership, apprenticeship), Immigration (2026-2028 levels plan), Major Projects (Fraser MPO commentary), and Promise Delivery (Angus Reid one-year review). The remaining PM Annex A trigger link was handled in the follow-up traceability repair.

summary: Recurring source checks now name event-driven watches, climate scans, promise spot-checks, and source-role review.

items.headline: Event-driven source watch list added
items.body: The recurring source checklist now calls out rating agencies, climate and carbon policy events, defence and NATO releases, major federal announcements, and bill-status movement as checks that should run when events appear instead of waiting for a fixed quarterly cadence.

items.headline: Long-tail source coverage made explicit
items.body: Climate and carbon sources, policy institutes, academic sources, journalism sources, stalled and abandoned promise links, source-role consistency, and archive fallback checks now have named rows in the recurring checklist rather than being hidden inside broad deep-search language.

items.headline: Public location wording removed
items.body: The About page now describes the project as independent without listing a project location.

summary: Source-coverage hygiene: the May refresh is now documented as a targeted refresh, not a full recertification.

items.headline: May source coverage ledger added
items.body: A new May source-coverage ledger records which source families were checked, which dimensions were refreshed, which pilot-packet links were spot-checked, and which gaps remain open. The May notes were also renamed from source-pull notes to source-refresh notes so the title matches the actual scope.

items.headline: Recurring source checklist created
items.body: A new recurring-source checklist defines the monthly, quarterly, and twice-yearly source checks for future cycles, plus the automation backlog for PBO RSS, StatCan value diffs, LEGISinfo, MPO diffs, polling pages, and Ethics Commissioner report changes.

items.headline: Inter-rater packet snapshot clarified
items.body: The pilot packet and reviewer invite now state that the rater is grading a frozen 2026-04-30 snapshot, not the current live dashboard. The results template now pre-fills the published snapshot grades to avoid comparing a rater against newer live data.

items.headline: Pilot source link spot-check completed
items.body: The 18 inter-rater packet source links were checked before recruitment. One broken House ETHI PDF link was replaced with the working House DocumentViewer report page in both the pilot packet and the live Ethics source list.

summary: May grade review: Fiscal Health moved up to C, Major Projects denominator was reconciled to the official MPO list, and Housing Supply kept D after the March starts check.

items.headline: Fiscal Health moved D → C
items.body: The Spring Economic Update lowered the projected FY 2025-26 deficit to $66.9B, and PBO now says both fiscal anchors are on track. The file stops at C because the deficit remains above the B threshold and PBO still flags capital-budgeting, interest-burden, and defence-cost caveats.
drivers: PBO says the deficit-to-GDP anchor is on track, declining from 2.1% in 2025-26 to 1.4% by 2030-31
PBO says the operating-balance anchor is projected to be met by 2028-29
Caveats remain on capital-budgeting definitions, rising interest burden, and omitted anticipated defence spending

items.headline: Fiscal-anchor promise moved back into progress
items.body: The operational-budget-balance promise now reads In Progress rather than Stalled. The evidence is still caveated: PBO says the anchors are on track, but also says the capital/operating classification needs more detail.

items.headline: Major Projects cohort denominator corrected to 15 projects
items.body: The official MPO page lists 15 referred projects and separates out transformative strategies. The dashboard now counts only the 15 projects in the cohort denominator; documented post-designation advancement remains 2 of 15, so the grade holds at C.

items.headline: Housing starts trigger reviewed and held
items.body: CMHC March 2026 starts showed a 235,852 monthly SAAR but a 248,378 six-month trend. Because CMHC says the trend measure smooths volatile monthly readings, the dashboard does not treat the one-month dip as firing the <240K down trigger while the trend remains above 240K.

summary: May source refresh: approval polling and several source metrics updated without changing grades.

items.headline: Approval Signal refreshed
items.body: Four recent approval polls from Abacus Data, Leger, and Angus Reid Institute were added. The 60-day sample-size-weighted display still rounds to 57% approve and 31% disapprove, net +26.

items.headline: Fiscal and labour metrics refreshed
items.body: Fiscal Health now uses the Spring Economic Update's $66.9B FY 2025-26 deficit projection and PBO's assessment that new measures offset most later fiscal room. Economic Policy now references the April Labour Force Survey.

items.headline: Affordability CPI refreshed
items.body: Affordability Response now uses March 2026 food-store CPI at 4.4% year over year. April CPI is scheduled for release on May 19.

items.headline: Manual review queue logged
items.body: The targeted source refresh flagged two calls for the grade-review phase: reconciling the Major Projects public project list with the live cohort, and deciding how the Housing Supply starts trigger should treat March CMHC starts data.

summary: Mobile evidence polish: the Major Projects full project list now uses readable project cards on phones.

items.headline: Major Projects list no longer needs sideways scrolling on mobile
items.body: The full project pipeline still uses the compact table on desktop, but phone-width screens now show stacked project cards with tranche, stage date, and source link visible in each card. No grades, scores, thresholds, source data, or methodology changed. The cohort denominator was later reconciled to 15 on 2026-05-13.

summary: Mobile card-spacing polish: dimension cards now have a little more breathing room while scrolling on phones.

items.headline: Scorecard cards breathe more on mobile
items.body: The mobile scorecard and tracker grids now use a wider gap between cards, responding to Reddit feedback that the grade cards felt cramped while scrolling. No grades, scores, sources, promise statuses, or methodology changed.

summary: Traceability polish: event-driven trigger sources now say so directly in the scoring drawer.

items.headline: Non-clickable trigger sources now identify event-driven evidence
items.body: Six grade-move triggers that depend on future events now label their source line as event-driven, so readers can distinguish evidence that already has a one-click source from evidence that would only exist if the trigger fires. No grades, scores, thresholds, source lists, or promise statuses changed.

summary: Scoring-boundary disclosure: the About and Methodology pages now state what the dashboard can and cannot score.

items.headline: About page now names the dashboard's scoring boundary
items.body: A new section explains that the dashboard scores sourceable federal action, documented commitments, published thresholds, and observable outcomes, not leadership style, symbolic politics, popularity, forecasts, or valuable outcomes that lack enough public evidence to grade.

items.headline: Methodology limits now address measurable-vs-valuable risk
items.body: The rubric limits now say plainly that the model can only score what can be inspected through public evidence, rather than estimating weakly evidenced qualities by proxy.

items.headline: README feature list reconciled with the live app
items.body: The removed Print / Export PDF feature is no longer advertised, and the About feature now mentions the new scoring-boundary disclosure.

summary: Mobile UX bug-fix bundle: trust frame is now global, evidence chips no longer clip on phones, drill-downs return readers to the scoreboard on close, and the project pipeline gives a clear scroll cue.

items.headline: What this is / what this isn't moved into the global header
items.body: The scope frame previously lived inside the Scorecard tab only. It now sits between the dashboard title and the scoreboard, so a reader who lands on Promises, Change Log, or Rubric still sees what the dashboard is and is not for.

items.headline: Print / Export PDF button removed
items.body: The button printed a screen-style page that was not optimized for paper. Removed alongside its print stylesheet rather than left as an unfulfilled promise.

items.headline: Promise tab evidence links no longer clip on mobile
items.body: Source and Status evidence chips on expanded promise rows now wrap their text instead of forcing a single line, so long source labels stay fully visible on narrow screens.

items.headline: Promise rows show a stronger details affordance
items.body: The previous pale chevron next to each promise now reads as a darker '▸ Details' / '▾ Hide' label so it is obvious that rows expand for evidence.

items.headline: Project pipeline now signals horizontal scroll
items.body: The Major Projects pipeline table now carries a 'Scroll right for stage date and source links →' caption and a right-edge fade gradient on narrow screens, so readers do not miss the source column.

items.headline: Tab rail signals overflow on narrow phones
items.body: On phones where 'Scorecard / Promises / Change Log / Rubric / About' overflows the rail, a small fade gradient on the right edge cues that more tabs sit off-screen.

items.headline: Closing a drill-down scrolls back to the scoreboard
items.body: On phones, hiding the score-derivation panel or the approval-signal drill-down now scrolls the page back to the scoreboard so readers do not have to manually backtrack.

items.headline: Evidence-link styling unified
items.body: Trigger-level evidence links and the project pipeline source column are now consistently rendered as 12px bold blue links, while file-level source chips remain the larger filled-chip treatment. Two visual treatments instead of five.

items.headline: Approval Signal card shares the same footer slot as the grade cards
items.body: 'See polls & sources' moved from the body of the Approval card into the footer slot, so all four scoreboard cards land their action affordance at the same vertical position.

items.headline: Trend arrows are now accessible
items.body: The improving / stable / declining arrows next to each dimension name now carry aria-labels and tooltips so the trend is announced to screen readers and visible on hover, not only via the legend.

items.headline: Duplicate freshness marker removed
items.body: Each dimension card showed both a 'Last reviewed' pill on the card face and an 'Updated YYYY-MM-DD' line above Key Metrics. The pill is now the single canonical freshness marker.

items.headline: Grade-change marker is now within the readable font floor
items.body: The '(was X)' previous-grade marker bumped from 11px to 12px so the mobile font-size floor catches it; the design tokens disallow body text below 12px.

summary: Mobile disclosure placement fix: headline-score and approval drill-downs now open directly under the tapped card on phones.

items.headline: Score math opens where mobile readers expect it
items.body: On narrow screens, the Household Impact and Full Policy Audit derivation panels now render immediately below the card that opened them instead of after all four headline boxes.

items.headline: Approval details follow the same mobile pattern
items.body: The Approval Signal drill-down now uses the same responsive ordering, so tapping the card scrolls to the poll details directly under that card on phones.

summary: Internal traceability pass: triggers whose evidence lives inside the dashboard now jump to their evidence home instead of remaining grey labels.

items.headline: Internal evidence homes are now clickable
items.body: Major Projects triggers can jump to the project pipeline, Flagship Delivery triggers can jump back to the home-dimension grid, and Promise Delivery triggers can open the Promises tab.

items.headline: Defence & Trade split tripwire tightened
items.body: The split rule now covers both opposite movement and widening sub-score gaps, and it explicitly uses two consecutive monthly review cycles as the promotion test.

items.headline: Ethics trigger language made more concrete
items.body: The governance-critique down-trigger now names the threshold directly: two or more listed governance sources must publish a material disclosure or screening gap finding.

items.headline: Promise Delivery stays visibly tracker-only
items.body: The expanded tracker card now shows its own trigger traceability without using grade language, and stale copy about future GPA removal was replaced with current tracker-only wording.

summary: Traceability cleanup follow-on: the audit now matches the live model, Defence & Trade carries an explicit split tripwire, and several easy trigger links were filled in.

items.headline: Consistency audit corrected to match the live tracker / scoring split
items.body: The new consistency self-audit no longer describes Promise Delivery as a live graded file. It now treats Promise Delivery as what the product already is: a derivative accountability tracker that sits outside the 11 performance grades.

items.headline: Defence & Trade now carries a visible split-promotion rule
items.body: The file still stays combined for now, but the methodology now says what breaks that structure: if the defence and trade sub-scores move in opposite directions for two consecutive review cycles, the split shadow promotes into live separate files.

items.headline: Another batch of trigger links was threaded
items.body: Climate, immigration, and housing now carry a few more direct trigger-source links where the public source home already existed, reducing the number of move conditions that still rely on label-only references.

items.headline: Promise Delivery no longer carries a live-grade field in current data
items.body: The tracker still keeps its internal accountability logic, but the live dimension data no longer exposes Promise Delivery as if it were a peer A–F score inside the current board.

summary: Traceability pass: grade-change triggers now carry their own source labels, exception files are framed more honestly, and source stacks are rebalanced into a tighter band.

items.headline: One-notch grade triggers now point at their own source homes
items.body: Move-up and move-down conditions are no longer just free-floating editorial text. Each trigger now carries its own source label, and where a public document exists, a direct source link appears immediately underneath it in the scoring drawer.

items.headline: Readers no longer have to infer which source backs which trigger
items.body: Expanded dimension cards now render a small source line under every one-notch trigger. That means the chain from grade to move condition to supporting source is shorter and more explicit than before.

items.headline: Thin and overloaded source stacks were rebalanced
items.body: Affordability Response, Housing Supply, and Promise Delivery now carry stronger public source trails, while Economic Policy Response was thinned back from a kitchen-sink stack to the same tighter 5-8 source band used elsewhere on the dashboard.

items.headline: Exception files are framed more honestly
items.body: Defence & Trade now explains why it remains one mixed file, and Flagship Delivery now identifies itself more clearly as a derived rollup instead of reading like a normal home dimension.

summary: Trust-feedback pass: the scorecard now explains what it is and is not for, makes freshness harder to miss, and shows where judgment enters each grade.

items.headline: Scorecard framing made explicit
items.body: The Scorecard view now opens with a compact plain-language note: this is a public performance scorecard built from thresholds, source links, and review dates; it is not a forecast, voting guide, popularity measure, or claim that only measurable files matter.

items.headline: Freshness is more visible
items.body: The header now treats the global Updated date as a visible badge, and each dimension's Last reviewed date is styled as a stronger review marker instead of a quiet italic footer.

items.headline: Judgment calls surfaced on every graded card
items.body: Each graded dimension now has a short card-face Judgment call line and a longer Where judgment enters explanation in the scoring drawer, so readers can separate source evidence, thresholds, and editor judgment.

items.headline: Mobile trust surfaces tightened
items.body: On narrow screens, the Scorecard framing now renders as a compact visible panel, Last reviewed pills use stronger contrast, and the Promises tab summary wraps cleanly so statuses like Abandoned are not clipped.

summary: Mobile scoreboard drill-downs now scroll into view, methodology shorthand was removed from the card surface, and the visitor counter is visible again with a same-origin fallback that no longer overlaps the mobile header.

items.headline: Visitor counter restored with a mobile-safe placement
items.body: The sitewide visitor count is back with a same-origin fallback, so browsers that block third-party analytics requests still show a real number instead of a missing badge. On phones, the badge now drops into normal flow above the title instead of floating over it.

items.headline: Headline-score panels now come into view on mobile
items.body: Tapping Household Impact, Full Policy Audit, or Approval Signal on a phone no longer leaves the opened detail panel far below the scoreboard strip. The dashboard now scrolls the panel into view automatically.

items.headline: Internal shorthand pills removed from dimension cards
items.body: Surface labels like "Credit-claiming penalty," "Sub-score file," and "Long-lag file" were removed from the card face. The underlying scoring logic still exists, but it now lives in the expanded explanation instead of reading like internal shorthand on the surface.

items.headline: Scoring adjustments rewritten in plainer language
items.body: Expanded card explanations now use reader-facing labels such as "External pressure," "Early-cycle adjustment," and "Credit reduced for overclaiming" instead of internal modifier names.

summary: Inspectability pass: headline scores now show their math, Major Projects is graded on cohort progress, and the scoring drawer carries a confidence / attribution / lag glossary.

items.headline: Headline scores now show how they're built
items.body: Both the Household Impact and Full Policy Audit cards have a new "How is this score built?" toggle. Click it and the dashboard shows the per-dimension grade, the points, the weight, and the arithmetic that produces the headline letter — so any reader can verify the score against the cards.

items.headline: Major Projects regraded on cohort progress, not first-event triggers
items.body: The Major Projects rubric now defines the project universe (16 projects across 3 MPO tranches as of April 2026) and grades on documented post-designation movement, not just promoted stage labels. The dimension card carries the full project list with each project's current stage and source link. As of 2026-04-30, 4 projects sit above designated status, but only 2 of 16 (~13%) show later-dated post-designation advancement in the recorded cohort data — which keeps the file at C.

items.headline: Confidence / Attribution / Lag glossary inside the scoring drawer
items.body: The three small pills at the top of every dimension's scoring drawer now sit above a one-click "What do these mean?" definition box: a one-sentence explanation each for confidence, attribution, and lag, with the level cutoffs spelled out (High / Medium / Low; Direct / Mixed / Mostly inherited; Short / Medium / Long / Event-driven).

summary: Methodology hardening pass: all dimensions now surface scoring logic, threshold language tightened, and Economic Policy / Ethics source gaps narrowed.

items.headline: Scoring drawers expanded across the dashboard
items.body: Every dimension now exposes its construct, threshold ladder, move triggers, and guardrails inside the card, instead of limiting that transparency to only three audited files.

items.headline: Threshold language tightened across the rubric
items.body: The rubric and canonical scoring sheets were rewritten to use more explicit counts, ranges, and decision rules, with less reliance on words like “credible,” “substantive,” or “material” standing alone.

items.headline: Economic Policy now tracks non-spending levers explicitly
items.body: The live file now surfaces business investment, tax competitiveness, internal-trade execution, regulatory-burden work, and permitting-adjacent checks alongside AI and critical-minerals funding.

items.headline: Ethics challenge stack broadened
items.body: Ethics & Transparency now includes the House ETHI report on the Conflict of Interest Act alongside Democracy Watch and official commissioner materials, reducing dependence on a single advocacy voice.

summary: Majority government confirmed, climate grade moved down to D, new public-approval signal at the top, and a readability pass across the dashboard.

items.headline: Climate & Environment moved D+ → D
items.body: Canada is tracking for about half of its required 2030 emissions reduction. Industrial carbon credits are trading near $20/t despite a $95 headline. ECCC is losing 840+ positions. The PM has acknowledged targets will be missed.
drivers: Industrial credits detached from headline price

items.headline: Majority government confirmed
items.body: Carney's Liberals won 3 Toronto/Quebec byelections on April 13, 2026, reaching 174 seats and securing a majority in the House of Commons.

items.headline: Federal gas tax suspension announced
items.body: Federal fuel excise suspended April 20 through September 7, 2026. Estimated $2.4B in foregone revenue over the window.

items.headline: Approval Signal added to the top of the dashboard
items.body: 60-day rolling average of approve/disapprove across five included pollsters (Léger, Abacus, Ipsos, Angus Reid Institute, Innovative Research). Tracked beside the grades but explicitly not one of them — popularity is not performance.

items.headline: Readability pass on the dashboard
items.body: Plainer card labels, shorter status lines, a new "Limits of this model" note in the Rubric tab, a per-dimension "Last reviewed" line, and an across-the-board font-size bump for mobile.
